_note: Past spaceflight fires used by the Incident Analyst agent (pyra/agents). Each one is broken into the same fire chain links. The text is a short summary of the cited NASA page; none of it has been checked by the team yet (verified_by is empty). Open the source, confirm every line, add access_date and put your name in verified_by, the same way as sources/sources.csv. The 'features' block is what the agent compares with a scenario, and it is our own reading of the source (INTERPRETATION).

incidents.name: Apollo 1
incidents.setting: ground test on the launch pad

chain.oxidizer: Pure oxygen cabin above sea-level pressure
chain.fuel: Nylon netting, hook-and-loop fasteners and foam pads
chain.ignition: Probable electrical arc from damaged wiring
chain.escape: Inward-opening hatch could not be opened against cabin pressure

incidents.name: Apollo 13
incidents.outcome: An oxygen tank failed; the crew returned using the lunar module.

chain.fuel: Teflon wire insulation inside the tank
chain.ignition: Heater switches damaged before launch; insulation burned when the tank fans ran
chain.detection: A bang and a pressure drop
chain.escape: Lunar module used as a lifeboat

incidents.name: Mir
incidents.outcome: The fire was put out; no lasting harm to the crew.

chain.fuel: Canister contents; a contaminant was the likely cause
chain.ignition: The canister failed when it was activated
chain.detection: Crew saw it; smoke filled the station
chain.suppression: Extinguishers; the flame went out on its own
chain.escape: The flame blocked the route to one docked return vehicle
